commons-nesting-check.desc: Verifies that no commons modules (see import-rules check) are nested (i.e. a `t` module having a `t`, `c`, `s`, `cnst` or `ext_traits` submodule like, for example, `/t/foo/c`).
commons-nesting-check.rationale: Make reasoning about commons modules easier

exception.desc: `c` commons modules may live inside parent `c` commons modules (e.g. `/c/foo/c/bar`). There may be as much nesting of these as desired.
exception.rationale: It's commonly necessary to nest `c` commons modules to share code within a `c` module.
